summary.text: Bayes' theorem is a rule for inverting conditional probabilities, so the probability of a cause can be found from its effect.
For example, it finds the chance a patient has a disease given a positive test, using the chance that the test is positive when the disease is present.
One of its applications is Bayesian inference, where it turns the probability of observations given a model into the probability of the model given the observations.

facts.label: Named after
facts.value: Thomas Bayes, a minister, statistician and philosopher

facts.label: First published
facts.value: 1763, in An Essay Towards Solving a Problem in the Doctrine of Chances

facts.label: Independent developer
facts.value: Pierre-Simon Laplace, working apart from Bayes

facts.label: Editor of the essay
facts.value: Richard Price, who edited the manuscript for two years

items.prompt: You know how often the pavement is wet on days when it rained. You want to know how likely it is that it rained, given that you see a wet pavement. What kind of rule does that job?

options.label: A rule that inverts a conditional probability
A rule that averages many wet days together
A rule that adds the two chances up directly
A rule that ignores the wet pavement entirely

items.explain: Bayes' theorem inverts conditional probabilities, letting you find the probability of a cause given its effect.

items.prompt: Besides Thomas Bayes, who developed this theorem on their own in the 18th century?

options.label: Richard Price, who edited Bayes's papers
Harold Jeffreys, who wrote a 1973 book
Pierre-Simon Laplace, working independently
Alan Turing, in the early 1940s

items.explain: Laplace developed it independently of Bayes. Price edited Bayes's manuscript, and Jeffreys and Turing came much later.

items.prompt: Thomas Bayes died leaving an unpublished manuscript. What happened to it next?

options.label: It was lost until Laplace rediscovered it
Bayes's family published it as it stood
A friend returned it to the Royal Society unread
Richard Price edited it for two years and sent it on

items.explain: Bayes's family gave his papers to Richard Price, who edited the manuscript for two years before sending it to John Canton, who read it aloud at the Royal Society.

items.prompt: Some writers say the result should really be called the Bayes-Price rule. What is their reasoning?

options.label: Price had the idea years before Bayes did
Price found Bayes's work, corrected it and found a use for it
Price proved Bayes's version wrong and replaced it
Price was the first to apply it to roulette wheels

items.explain: The argument is that Price discovered Bayes's work, recognized its importance, corrected it, contributed to the article and found a use for it.

items.prompt: Working apart from Bayes, Laplace used conditional probability to connect two quantities, given some evidence. Which two?

options.label: A prior probability and an updated posterior probability
A sample mean and a population mean
A binomial distribution and a normal one
A winning streak and a losing streak

items.explain: Laplace formulated the relation of an updated posterior probability to a prior probability, given evidence.

items.prompt: In the notation P(A | B), what does the vertical bar tell you?

options.label: A is divided by B
The chance of A occurring given that B is true
The chance of A and B happening together
The chance of A or B happening

items.explain: P(A | B) is a conditional probability: the probability of event A occurring given that B is true.
